:::{#exm-cholesky}
#### Two Cholesky factors

- $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 \\ 2 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \ell_{11} &= \sqrt{4} \\
  &= 2,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \ell_{21} &= 2/2 \\
  &= 1,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  and

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \ell_{22}^2 &= 5 - 1^2 \\
  &= 4,
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  so $\ell_{22} = 2$:
  $\matr{L} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$, and

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \matr{L} \tp{\matr{L}} &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \cd 2 & 2 \cd 1 \\ 1 \cd 2 & 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd 2 \end{bmatrix} \\
  &= \matr{A}.
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\begin{bmatrix} 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5 \end{bmatrix}$:
  $\ell_{11} = \sqrt{5}$, $\ell_{21} = 4/\sqrt{5}$,
  and

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \ell_{22}^2 &= 5 - \tfrac{16}{5} \\
  &= \tfrac{9}{5},
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  the Schur complement of @exm-schur-complement,
  so $\ell_{22} = \tfrac{3}{\sqrt{5}}$.
- For $\matr{D} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ the method breaks down:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \ell_{22}^2 &= 1 - 4 \\
  &= -3
  \end{aligned}
  $$

  has no real solution,
  matching the failure of the Schur complement test (@exm-schur-test).

:::
